item.title: Didgeridoo 2.0.0
item.description:
• MIDI learn: every knob listens to a MIDI controller (CC). Click MIDI in the header to see the controllers; click a knob and move a control to give it to the knob. A double click gives a knob back the controller it came with, a secondary click can take it away, Defaults puts all back.
  • Every knob comes with a controller: Volume 7, Glide 5, Vowel 11 (an expression pedal opens the mouth), Drive 2 (a breath controller), Buzz 70, Tongue 71, Release 72, Attack 73, Tone 74, LFO 1 Rate 76, and for the others 20 to 31, 85 to 90, 102 and 103 (the manual has the list). A controller's 0 is the bottom of the knob's travel and 127 the top; 64 puts Rhy>Vowel on its middle. The mod wheel and the sustain pedal do what they did.
  • The plug-in answers the same controllers when a host passes them on, and the host saves them with the project; the app remembers them between launches.
  • Two LFOs can move the knobs. Each has a Rate (0.02 to 20 Hz) and a Shape (Sine, Triangle, Ramp Up, Ramp Down, Square, Steps, Wander); their four knobs are in Mouth. Click LFO 1 or LFO 2 in the header and the knobs set how far that LFO moves them: drag for the amount (down for a negative one), double-click to put it back. An arc on a knob shows what an LFO sweeps. Sixteen knobs can be moved, by both LFOs at once. The amounts are stored with the sound, and a host sees each as a parameter ("LFO 1>Vowel").
  • Wobble Rate and Wobble Depth are gone: Wobble is LFO 1 on Vowel now, and the programs keep their movement.
  • The instrument is now one model, built on the measurements of real didgeridoos, and no longer a synthesizer with those measurements beside it. Every program sounds different from 1.0.x. This is a deliberate departure from the MPC plugin "Didgeridoo", whose synthesis it replaces.
    • Lips: the source is the air that passes lips which are shut for part of every cycle. Buzz sets how hard they close (it used to narrow a pulse); Drive is how hard they are blown and works on the lips themselves (it used to distort the finished sound, which also filled in the notches of the tongue).
    • Mouth: only the tongue is left. Vowel says where the tongue stands and Tongue how deep it cuts. Formant and Reso are gone: they added peaks where a real mouth takes sound away.
    • Tube: eight resonances, placed by how much the tube flares (the new knob Flare). Body is gone; the tube's first resonance does its work. Tone moved here.
    • Voice: one sung voice with a list of intervals that lock to the drone (Voice Pitch: Unison to Twelfth, the tenth as it comes) and a new knob, Rough, that pulls it off the lock so that it beats. Growl and Growl Pitch are gone; aftertouch now adds Voice.
    • Breath passes the lips, so its noise comes in bursts at the drone's pitch.
  • The overblown note is gone. A hard hit is a loud drone; Toot Vel and Toot Len are gone, and so is the ochre band on the keys of the app's keyboard, whose bottom is now simply the hardest hit. Toot Pitch, which also set the tube's shape, is now the knob Flare: 0 % is a plain pipe, higher values a tube that widens towards its end.
  • As it comes, the instrument has the tube and the tongue on, Drift at 12 % and Bend Range at 1 semitone. Volume rests at 0 dB.
  • 30 knobs instead of 33. The ten programs keep their names and were voiced again.
  • Sounds stored by 1.0.x are not carried over: the app starts with Classic Drone, and a host project saved with the 1.0.x plug-in restores wrong values, so choose a program again. Several knobs kept their name and changed their meaning.
  • Turning Buzz, Drive or Voice while a note sounds makes no click.
